union.summary: No test for the top-level lone-dash setext heading whose rendering this change breaks (`Heading\n-`), even though the change's own plan lists it as a required test case
union.evidence:
The new `lheadingRule` in list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts rejects ANY lone single `-` underline (`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1`), not just one indented under a list item, and `wrappedList` then lets that dash terminate the paragraph in silent mode whenever `state.parentType === 'paragraph'`. So the very common top-level form `Heading -` changes from `

Heading

` to a paragraph followed by an empty `
` — a user-visible behavior change with zero coverage. The five tests added (preview.test.ts +151..+196) cover only: `- 1 -`, `- 1 - `, `- 1 - `, `Heading ---`, `- 1 - 2`. The change's own TODO file admits the gap: docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md line 61 says `- [ ] Unit tests in preview.test.ts (bug case, workaround, --- setext still works, non-empty nested list unaffected, top-level lone dash)` — the box is unchecked and the top-level lone-dash case never appears in the diff. Because the behavior is newly changed, a pre-existing test could not already assert it (it would now fail and would have had to be updated in this diff).

union.summary: No test for an over-indented / code-block-indent empty bullet, where the silent hook claims paragraph termination without the 4-space guard the real list rule applies
union.evidence: `wrappedList` returns `true` in silent mode purely on `isEmptyBulletLine`, which checks only `state.sCount[line] >= state.blkIndent` and never the `sCount - blkIndent >= 4` code-block guard that the stock `list` rule applies. So input such as `1\n    -` (or an empty bullet indented far past the parent item) now terminates the paragraph even though the non-silent `list` rule will decline the line, and the line falls through to the indented-code rule instead. None of the added tests use more than two spaces of indentation, so this divergence between the silent claim and the non-silent outcome has no coverage.
